question: Is a pivot cheap enough to be the common path, and what does superseding a decision mean?
kill: a pivot needs more than one command or a dialog
head: e31895d54033144d873f463b5242ce27350a9c37

directions.text: pivot as one command: close the direction with a learned line, mark superseded decisions, open the next, print the boundary

entries.text: code: cmd_pivot in scripts/spike.py takes the new direction, --learned and --supersedes D1,D2; it closes the direction, stamps superseded_by with the NEW direction's number, opens the next, re-renders all three files and prints the parked questions and open decisions so the boundary is visible.

measured: in tests/live.sh a sonnet session ran /spike:pivot for $0.16 in 3 turns and wrote its own learned line from the log without being given one; the live run on 2026-10-30 passed all pivot checks.

code: supersession is by direction number, not by a replacement decision id. The reversed decision stays in decisions.md and in the handoff table with 'superseded by: direction N'; a reader treats it as history. A new decision for the new direction is recorded separately when it is settled.
should a pivot commit the spike branch automatically when the tree is dirty, so the direction's pointer is never lost?
a superseded decision is kept, marked with the direction that reversed it, never deleted or rewritten

directions.learned: one command is enough; the boundary print is what makes the pivot safe, not a dialog

directions.text: should --learned be mandatory at the script level?

entries.text: tried: making --learned required in argparse. It would refuse a pivot when a direction taught nothing, which is itself worth writing down; the skill demands the line and the script renders '(nothing recorded)' when it is absent, so the gap is visible instead of blocking.

found: in spike handoff-format the handoff's head pointer equals its base because close, handoff and the commit happened in one step. The close skill commits before handoff and the handoff skill commits after, so in the normal flow head is the close commit; recorded here rather than silently fixed.
--learned stays optional in the script and mandatory in the skill; an empty learned line renders visibly
